first_impression.reaction: I searched 'bali wedding venues' half expecting Instagram fluff, and Bali can feel a bit cheap to our friends. The intro splits the island into four areas and says it's not a ranking. No 'paradise', no 'dream day', so I kept going. The table and the guest-count grid are the bits I'd actually use. But it reads like a very tidy spec sheet: lots of 'Not published' and 'ask in writing', no prices, no real wedding, and nothing that tells me which of these feels personal rather than like a resort package.

journey.quote: The right one depends on how many guests are flying in, the ceremony you want and the setting you want behind you as you say your vows.
journey.reaction: Starts with guest numbers, which is our actual problem. Sensible framing.

journey.quote: Only a few venues publish a full resort buy-out, including Samabe and the two COMO properties, so ask every venue the same questions about exclusive use in writing.
journey.reaction: Two COMO properties? I only ever found one COMO in the list. Small thing, but it makes me wonder what else is off.

journey.section: Bali wedding venues at a glance
journey.quote: "Not published" means the venue does not state the detail.
journey.reaction: Then nearly every row in the exclusive-use column says 'Not published'. Honest, but the column tells me almost nothing.

journey.quote: A 60-guest ceremony fits Tresna Chapel, but a seated dinner for the same group needs a second space, so plan the move between them into the timeline.
journey.reaction: This is the insider-ish detail I want. 60 is roughly our number, and I wouldn't have spotted that.

journey.quote: One couple featured in the resort's own wedding story married at the fountain and held their reception at Akasa.
journey.reaction: So the only real wedding on the page is the resort's own marketing, not one you planned. I want yours.

journey.quote: The ceremony is a celebrant blessing at The villa, which the venue describes as non-legal, with a commemorative wedding certificate.
journey.reaction: Good that it's flagged. Exactly the kind of trap I'd hate to discover late.

journey.quote: With 32 villas, whether your guests can fill the resort is a fair question to ask.
journey.reaction: Honest trade-off, and relevant with 40 of our guests flying in. Wish it went one step further and said where the rest would stay.

journey.section: Guest count, rooms and exclusive use
journey.quote: Use this table to narrow by guest numbers. Each figure is the venue's own, for the space named.
journey.reaction: Most useful bit of the page. I can see our 60 to 90 band immediately. Sending this to James.

journey.section: Guest count, rooms and exclusive use
journey.quote: Anything this guide marks "Not published", from capacity to exclusive use, needs an answer in writing before you commit, and your Wedded Advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you sign, through [Wedded Concierge]
journey.reaction: Reassuring on hidden costs. But there's not one price anywhere in a venue guide. Not even a From AUD range for a Bali wedding of our size. Dad will ask first thing.

journey.section: How do guests get to Bali and between the areas?
journey.quote: Damaged passports, including water damage or minor tears, have led to refused entry, so ask guests to check theirs early.
journey.reaction: Didn't know that. Going straight in the guest info pack.

journey.section: How do guests get to Bali and between the areas?
journey.quote: Does the venue arrange guest transport, and for how many guests?
journey.reaction: My biggest worry is grandparents from the airport, and it's handed back to us as a list of questions. Only one drive time on the whole page, for Ubud. Nothing for Uluwatu or Nusa Dua.

journey.section: When is the right time to get married in Bali?
journey.quote: There have been cases of methanol poisoning in Bali, so serve and order only branded alcohol.
journey.reaction: Honest and useful, but Mum reads the volcano, tsunami, rabies, dengue and methanol list and Bali is off the table. No sense of which months are actually best.

journey.section: Can foreigners legally marry in Bali?
journey.quote: Persons of any nationality may generally marry in Indonesia if they hold a religion recognised by the Indonesian Government, listed as Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism or Christian, and both parties must hold the same religion.
journey.reaction: Important. James isn't religious. So realistically we'd do the legal bit in Sydney and a symbolic ceremony here? Clear enough to work that out, but I'd like it said.

journey.section: Shortlist your Bali venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
journey.reaction: AUD and one person are the right reassurances, and no hard sell. Still the usual end-to-end line: who is on the ground in Bali on the day?

unanswered_questions: Roughly what does a Bali wedding for 60 to 90 guests cost, even as a From AUD range?
How long are transfers from Ngurah Rai to Uluwatu, Nusa Dua, Jimbaran and Seminyak?
Which months are best for older guests, given the wet season runs around October to April?
If we don't share a recognised religion, is the usual path a legal marriage at home plus a symbolic ceremony in Bali?
Which of these venues let you make it feel personal rather than a hotel package (outside vendors, styling)?
Which second COMO property does the takeaways line mean?
Do you have a real Bali wedding (venue, date) we can look at? (deferred business detail)
Who is on the ground in Bali on the day: your own person or a local partner? (deferred business detail)
Do you arrange guest airport transfers, including for grandparents? (deferred business detail)
How does Wedded Wonderland charge: flat fee, percentage, commissions? (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: Anything this guide marks "Not published", from capacity to exclusive use, needs an answer in writing before you commit
turn_offs_found.why: Vague pricing with no ranges: a whole venue guide with no cost figure at all feeds our hidden-costs and currency fear.

turn_offs_found.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
turn_offs_found.why: 'Start to finish' is the generic end-to-end claim. It doesn't say who is accountable in Bali on the day or whether local work is outsourced to strangers.

turn_offs_found.quote: One couple featured in the resort's own wedding story married at the fountain and held their reception at Akasa.
turn_offs_found.why: The only real-wedding evidence is the venue's own marketing, not a Wedded Wonderland wedding with venue and date, which is the trust signal we need before enquiring.

would_share_with: James: the 'Guest count, rooms and exclusive use' table and the AYANA Tresna Chapel note, because they narrow venues to our 60 to 90 guests
My parents: the 'Can foreigners legally marry in Bali?' section, because Dad will ask if it's legal at home. I would not send the hazards list to Mum yet

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [shortlist your Bali venues through Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=bali-wedding-venues&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: Calm, no pressure, AUD and fee in writing are right. But no price range, few transfer times and no real Bali wedding of yours. I'd read one more post and want to see a real wedding before enquiring.

top_3_changes: Give us a cost anchor: the line 'Anything this guide marks "Not published"... needs an answer in writing' is honest, but add at least a From AUD range (with sign-off) or say plainly how we get venue pricing.
Answer the grandparents question: 'Does the venue arrange guest transport, and for how many guests?' hands it back to us. Add rough airport transfer times for each area, not just Ubud.

Fix 'the two COMO properties' in the takeaways (only COMO Uma Ubud appears), and link a real Wedded Wonderland Bali wedding with venue and date to replace the resort's own story as the only real-wedding evidence.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Sophie & James (planner couple): skimmed, looked for guest numbers, transfers, legal confidence, hidden costs and accountability
No invented brand facts; fees, on-the-ground team, real weddings and transfers listed as deferred unanswered questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored

open_questions.question: Key takeaways says 'the two COMO properties' but only COMO Uma Ubud is in the guide. Is a second COMO missing or is the line wrong?
Is a From AUD range available for sign-off for a Bali venue guide?

assumptions: Sophie & James arrived via a Google search for 'bali wedding venues' with Bali as one early option, so relevance is 4 and enquiry likelihood 2 (they enquire after 2 to 3 posts plus a real wedding).
Business details and fee amounts are deferred and not penalised as must-fix.
Fast-mode read: skimmed venue profiles, read the intro, tables, transport, weather, legal and close; FAQ skimmed.
